args: In libxml2/valid.c, analyze xmlAddRef's decision to retain xmlAttr versus copy attr->name during streaming validation. What reliable context field or condition identifies xmlTextReader/SAX streaming validation even before the first element is pushed and vstateNr becomes nonzero? Also explain ownership/freeing of xmlRef fields and suggest the smallest root-cause fix, including compatibility implications for normal tree validation.

The reported ASan UAF occurs in xmlTextReader mode with DTD validation. SAX attribute validation invokes xmlAddRef for the root/first element while xmlValidCtxt.vstateNr is zero. xmlAddRef then retains ret->attr = attr, but xmlTextReader incremental cleanup frees that property and its name; final unresolved IDREF checking dereferences it. Existing behavior apparently copies attr->name when vstateNr != 0. I need identify an established streaming-mode marker in xmlValidCtxt or its callbacks and ensure cleanup correctly distinguishes copied names from attr pointers. Relevant source is libxml2/valid.c; reader logic is likely libxml2/xmlreader.c.
